answer: Split tasks between strangers. Each epoch the network pairs random identities and gives each half of a puzzle, like two pages of one atlas, solvable only by talking over a logged channel. Real strangers need several rounds. Personas run by one operator often hold both pages and finish after a hollow, too-short chat. The bigger the farm, the more often its personas get paired, so flags pile up and stakes freeze. Dodging it means walling off every persona's memory, the cost of running real agents. Like an orchard where each tree must show its own roots.
